name: Ethiopian Doro Wat
description: Doro wat, chicken slow-simmered in a deep red berbere sauce, is widely considered Ethiopia's national dish - real berbere, a complex chili-and-spice blend, is what gives it its actual identity, not a generic chili powder.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion alone in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 12-15 minutes, until deeply softened and reduced - real doro wat cooks the onion this long before any fat is added, which is what builds its base flavor.
Add the ghee and garlic, cooking 1 minute, then stir in the berbere and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and a splash of water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until the chicken is very tender and the sauce is deep red and thick.
Add the whole hard-boiled egg in the last 10 minutes to absorb the sauce.

name: Ethiopian Misir Wat
description: Misir wat, red lentils simmered in a berbere-spiced sauce, a genuine Ethiopian staple, especially common during fasting periods.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat, 8-9 minutes, until softened.
Add the garlic and berbere, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the lentils and 1.5 cups water, and simmer 20-22 minutes until the lentils are tender and the sauce has thickened.

name: Ethiopian Injera-Style Flatbread
description: Injera, a spongy, slightly sour flatbread made from fermented teff, is the foundation of Ethiopian eating, used both as plate and utensil - a full days-long ferment is what gives real injera its distinctive tang and texture, which this quicker version can only approximate.
steps_detailed: Whisk the teff flour, all-purpose flour, vinegar, and 1 cup water into a thin, smooth batter.
Let sit at room temperature at least 6-8 hours, or overnight, to develop some tang - real injera ferments for several days, so this shortcut version will be milder.
Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled non-stick pan and cook, covered, without flipping, 2-3 minutes, until bubbles cover the surface and the edges lift.

name: Ethiopian Kitfo
description: Kitfo, minced raw or lightly warmed beef seasoned with berbere and spiced clarified butter, is a genuine Ethiopian delicacy.
steps_detailed: Warm the ghee gently and stir in the berbere.
Toss the minced beef with the warm spiced butter just until barely warmed through, keeping it rare - traditional kitfo is often served raw or barely cooked.

Add the onion, pepper, garlic, and rosemary, and cook 5-6 minutes more until the vegetables are tender-crisp.

name: Ethiopian Shiro
description: Shiro, a smooth, spiced chickpea flour stew, is one of Ethiopia's most common everyday dishes, especially during fasting periods.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil, 6-7 minutes, then add the garlic and berbere, cooking 1 minute.
Whisk the chickpea flour with 1.5 cups water until smooth, then stir into the pot.
Simmer, stirring often, 10-12 minutes, until thickened and smooth.
